learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how biological catalysts (enzymes) speed up the chemistry of life, and how energy flows through cellular systems!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Enzymes are mostly proteins (though some RNA molecules called ribozymes act as enzymes). They act as biocatalysts that speed up chemical reactions without being consumed in the process.
Activation energy is the 'push' needed to start a reaction. Enzymes lower this energy barrier, making the reaction happen much faster and easier at normal body temperatures.

Every enzyme has an 'active site' with a specific shape. Only a specific reactant (substrate) can fit into it perfectly, just like a specific key fits into a specific lock. (Or the newer Induced Fit model, where it molds around the substrate).

Enzyme activity is highly sensitive to Temperature and pH. Extreme heat denatures (destroys) the protein structure. Extreme pH can alter the active site. Substrate concentration also affects the rate up to a saturation point (Vmax).
Bioenergetics is the study of energy flow in living systems. ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell. Breaking the phosphate bonds in ATP releases energy for cellular work.

fun_activity.title: 🔥 The High Jump
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you have to jump over a 6-foot wall to get home (High Activation Energy). An enzyme acts like a trampoline placed right in front of the wall, allowing you to bounce right over with ease!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate between competitive and non-competitive inhibitors. Competitive binds to the active site; non-competitive binds elsewhere (allosteric site) and changes the enzyme's shape.
📌 All enzymes are proteins, but not all proteins are enzymes. (Remember the exception: Ribozymes are RNA!).
📌 Draw the graph showing how enzymes lower activation energy—it's a guaranteed high-scoring visual for your exams.
quick_recap: ⭐ The combination of an enzyme and its substrate forms a temporary Enzyme-Substrate (ES) complex.
⭐ Denaturation is the loss of a protein's 3D structure due to high heat, causing it to lose its function permanently.
⭐ Energy is neither created nor destroyed in biological systems; it is just transformed (e.g., light energy to chemical energy in photosynthesis).
